show_title: Capital Allocators – Inside the Institutional Investment Industry
title: REPLAY - Scott Malpass – The Fighting Irish's Twelfth Man (Capital Allocators, EP.25)

reader_summary.headline: I'm Ted Sides, and this is Capital Allocators.
reader_summary.overview: I'm Ted Sides, and this is Capital Allocators. This show is an open exploration of the people and process behind capital allocation. Through conversations with leaders in the money game, we learn how these holders of the keys to the kingdom allocate their time and their capital.

key_points.text: My guest on today's show is Scott Malpass, the esteemed vice president, and chief investment officer of Notre Dame.
key_points.evidence_quote: My guest on today's show is Scott Malpass, the esteemed vice president, and chief investment officer of Notre Dame, where he oversees the university's $12 billion endowment.

key_points.text: Scott earned his BA and MBA degrees at Notre Dame and returned to South Bend at the right age of 26.
key_points.evidence_quote: Scott earned his BA and MBA degrees at Notre Dame and returned to South Bend at the right age of 26, following a brief stint on Wall Street.

key_points.text: His track record for almost 30 years, as defined by both performance and impact.
key_points.evidence_quote: His track record for almost 30 years, as defined by both performance and impact, place him indisputably in rare company at the very top of the field.

thesis: Scott Malpass argues that Notre Dame's investment team possesses an unusual amount of duration and deep commitment because the university's stable leadership structure and Catholic mission draw alumni who stay for the mission rather than seeking career advancement elsewhere. He contrasts this philosophy with the Yale model, noting that his core team consists of Notre Dame graduates who are motivated by the tangible impact their work has on financial aid and the campus community.
